packs.title: Lakes, Gardens and Neighborhoods
packs.promise: Explore Madison's gardens, lakefront parks, wildlife and reused places across separate outings.

q.s: Sketch how a former feed-mill building serves a public gathering use today.
st: View the open public hall or the operator's building images.
Sketch one retained industrial form and one present-day public-use area.
Label which detail comes from direct observation and which from the operator history.

q.s: Compare one zoo habitat feature with its animal-care or conservation explanation.
st: Choose one open habitat or operator exhibit image.
Describe a visible shelter, movement space or enrichment feature without guessing an animal's feelings.
Record a separate operator-sourced care or conservation point.

q.s: Identify two different access features in Warner Park's public playground.
st: Use the public playground's open perimeter or city park images.
Find two features intended to help different visitors participate.
Record each feature and the city's description without judging a person's ability.

packs.title: Capitol to Campus
packs.promise: Follow connected civic, arts and campus-edge public places in two afternoons.

q.s: Use the Capitol's four wings to make a lawful orientation plan for the Square.
st: Find the Capitol's four-wing plan on site or in its official guide.
Choose two different public exits or exterior approaches toward the Square.
Draw a short orientation sketch showing the two directions and a controlled crossing.

q.s: Plan a public library visit around a service that needs no card or program booking.
st: Find the Central Library's address and current hours in its branch guide.
Choose one public reading, reference or making space described by the operator.
Record a two-step visit plan and a closed-hours version using the same guide.

q.s: Diagram the public hill's view back toward State Street and the Capitol.
st: Find an open outdoor viewpoint or UW's published hilltop image.
Draw the relation between the hill, State Street direction and distant Capitol.
Mark one place where a visitor should choose an accessible alternate path rather than assume the slope is easy.
